inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report note 3.2 'Share based payment expense' nil (FY2024: $804k); FY25 LTI was cash-settled. SBC-zero market per owner-fcf.md s7(e): SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases FY2023-FY2026 (financing activities). No ordinary dividend since the FY2024 interim; policy is >=70% of adjusted NPAT, which was a loss in FY2025.
inputs.share_count_basis: 345,354k ordinary shares net of treasury (FY2025 Annual Report EPS note, weighted average = period-end, unchanged since FY2022; H1 FY2026 basic = diluted EPS 4.6c). No dilutive instruments: FY25/FY26 LTI is cash-settled. Held FLAT; SBC is nil so there is nothing to double-count.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-21T04:15:20Z NZX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime via make dcf-context)
inputs.balance_sheet_source: H1 FY2026 interim financial statements (26 weeks to 1-Feb-2026, released 27-Mar-2026): cash 43,264k, borrowings 136,570k, lease liabilities 708,861k, minority interest 1,108k
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The FULL IFRS-16 lease cash (FY2025: principal $104.882m in financing + interest $36.847m in operating = $141.729m, 4.6% of revenue; H1 FY2026 $64.570m) is deducted inside the flow build as a dollar premises bill ($140m FY2026E escalating 2%/yr, expressed per scenario as lease_cost_pct_path), and lease liabilities ($708.9m at 1-Feb-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. net_debt = borrowings $136.570m less cash $43.264m = $93.306m, which ties to the company's own note 13 'Net cash/(debt)' (93,306). D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: $156.5m total less $93.3m ROU = $63.2m, 2.05% of revenue), so the lease is charged once. core_metrics.total_debt already excludes leases, so the CSV and the DCF are on the same basis.
inputs.net_debt_note: 1-Feb-2026 borrowings are inflated by balance-date timing (month-end creditor/GST payments fell after balance date; average daily borrowings were $79.5m vs $131.5m pcp per note 13). FY2025 year-end net debt was $96.1m. The latest filed figure ($93.3m) is used unadjusted; seasonal working-capital swings of +/-$100m between H1 and FY are normal for this retailer.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD flows discounted at a NZD-built rate. Bottom-up: NZ 10y govt ~4.4% + beta 1.25 (NZX cyclical discretionary retailer, mkt cap ~NZ$207m) x 5.5% ERP = 11.3% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~4.7% (BKBM + margin, 28% tax); 30% debt / 70% equity ex-lease => 9.3%. The company's own FY2025 impairment tests use 11.1-11.7% post-tax. House rate 10.0%, the midpoint, applied to ALL THREE scenarios: cyclicality, competitive erosion and covenant risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (owner-fcf.md s7f).
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US cyclical consumer retailer -> owner-fcf.md + section 7 adaptations). Fresh build; no prior WHS.NZ DCF and no MEMORY.md entry. 10-year explicit horizon because the lease-adjusted margin is still recovering from a cyclical trough; component-built margins; Gordon/12x cap terminal (cyclical cap per s4).

OWNER FCF (treatment B): last_fcf = reported FCF 59.719 - lease principal 104.882 - SBC 0 - interest income 0.319 = -45.482 (FY2025). TTM to H1 FY2026 = -112.4. Both are dominated by working-capital swings (FY25 payables -84.2m, H1 FY26 inventory -43.6m) and are NOT the projection base; the component build anchors on lease-adjusted EBITDA (FY25 $55.3m, TTM $57.0m, 1.8% of revenue) less ex-ROU D&A, curtailed capex ($12.6m vs ex-ROU D&A $63.2m) normalising to 2% of revenue, and NZ$121m of gross tax losses.

INTEREST INCOME: $0.319m FY2025 is immaterial and the company is net debt; not stripped (set to 0). Bank interest expense ($7.0m FY25) is a financing cost handled through WACC, not deducted from the flows.
NCI: 50% of ChocolateWorks; profit share $0.337m FY25. Charged once, in the bridge, at book value $1.108m (1-Feb-2026).

TIMING: FY2026 (52 weeks) ended 2-Aug-2026 and the annual result is scheduled for 30-Sep-2026, nine days after this valuation. Year 1 of the model is FY2026E with H1 already realised (lease-adj EBITDA $51.9m; owner FCF $3.1m). ANALYSIS JSON: landed mid-build (2026-09-21 21:05) and was read before finalising. Two of its facts moved the drivers: (1) the Q3 FY26 trading update (13 weeks to 3-May-2026: sales -1.4%, gross margin +50bps, online 6.8%) plus FY2026 being 52 weeks against a 53-week FY2025 => year-1 revenue growth set to -2.0% base / -3.0% bear / -1.5% bull instead of +1.0%; (2) guided cost-reset savings of ~$17m annualised by FY2031 ($3-4m in FY26; ~$110m over two 5-year TCS terms) => base mature lease-adjusted EBITDA margin trimmed from 3.5% to 3.2% (cost-out ~0.55pp + gross-margin recovery ~0.5pp + modest leverage on 2% nominal growth). Bull/bear axes in the narratives match the Analysis JSON bull_case/bear_case lists (cost reset traction, units/basket growth, Warehouse Stationery vs. breakeven margins for three years, structural price competition, $709m fixed lease base, leadership churn).

SANITY MULTIPLES (lease-consistent): ex-lease EV = mkt cap 207.2 + net debt 93.3 = $300.5m = 5.3x TTM lease-adjusted EBITDA ($57.0m); lease-inclusive EV = $1,009m = 5.1x TTM post-IFRS-16 EBITDA ($197.6m). P/B 0.67x on $310.7m equity; NTA/share $0.527 (H1 FY26 announcement).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case nominal revenue growth (~NZ CPI, zero real): revenue has compounded at 0.4%/yr FY2018-FY2025 and -2.1%/yr over three years; equity CAGR is negative (-11.0% 3yr, -4.5% 5yr) and describes losses plus the FY2022-24 dividends, not forward growth; EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative endpoints)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-11.0% 3yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (-2.1% 3yr) by more than 30%: FY2024 net loss (-$54.2m incl. Torpedo7 disposal), FY2025 loss and $175m of dividends FY2022-24 shrank book value while sales were flat. Neither series is a usable forward growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (treatment B) FY2018-FY2025: 35.8, 135.8, 258.9, 63.7, -100.9, -3.6, 46.1, -45.5. FY2020 is a COVID artefact (wage subsidy $67.7m, deferred creditor payments); FY2022 reverses it. Lease-adjusted EBITDA margin: 3.9, 5.3, 4.2, 6.0, 5.2, 3.3, 2.7, 1.8% (median ~4.0%; TTM 1.85%). The FY2025 reported FCF ($59.7m) and OCF ($72.3m) already look weak, and after the $104.9m lease principal the owner series is negative -- capex of $12.6m against $63.2m ex-ROU D&A is also unsustainable and is normalised in every scenario.

scenario_narratives.bear: NZ discretionary spending stays weak through FY2027 (fuel/freight shock from the Middle East conflict flagged as a subsequent event, weak consumer confidence), Kmart's store roll-out and Temu/Shein take general-merchandise share from The Warehouse, and Noel Leeming's margin stays ~1-2% under JB Hi-Fi/Harvey Norman pressure. Reported revenue falls 3% in FY26 (52 vs 53 weeks plus the Q3 run-rate), slips again in FY27, then grows ~1% nominal (negative real), the cost reset only offsets wage inflation, so the lease-adjusted EBITDA margin never recovers from ~2%. Capex still has to normalise to ~1.7% of sales to keep 217 stores trading, so owner FCF trends to ~zero: the terminal value hits the zero floor and equity is worth less than the $93m of bank debt -- i.e. the business is a going concern only because the banks keep amending the interest-cover covenant (already reset twice, to 6.5x/7.5x operating-profit-plus-depreciation for FY26/FY27).
scenario_narratives.base: Partial mid-cycle recovery, not a return to the FY2019-22 margins. The Nov-2025 cost reset (TCS co-sourcing of technology, accounting, call centres and payroll; $4.8m redundancy; SSO costs already -7.8% in FY25) lifts the lease-adjusted EBITDA margin from 1.8% to 3.2% by FY2031 -- guided savings are only ~$17m annualised by FY2031, so the rest comes from the gross-margin recovery already visible in Q3 FY26 (+50bps) and modest operating leverage; 3.2% is below the 4.0% eight-year median and well below the company's own impairment-test terminal EBIT margins of 3.2-4.0% -- with FY2026 reported revenue ~2% lower (52 weeks vs 53, Q3 sales -1.4%) then ~2% nominal growth (zero real: store count still shrinking, 84 Warehouse stores vs 88 two years ago). Capex normalises from $12.6m to 2% of revenue, the $121m of tax losses shelter cash tax until FY2029, and working capital consumes 5c per dollar of growth. Owner FCF settles at ~$30m (0.8% margin) -- roughly the cost of capital on a $300m ex-lease EV, so the equity value is a modest premium to net assets.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cost reset delivers in full and the consumer cycle turns: OCR cuts restore NZ discretionary spending in FY2027-28, The Warehouse's private-label/grocery mix and 1-hour click-and-collect hold share against Kmart and Temu, Noel Leeming's operating margin returns to ~3% and Warehouse Stationery holds ~7% (H1 FY26 already 7.0%). After the 52-week FY26 (-1.5%), revenue grows 3-3.5% for three years, the lease-adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 4.5% (post-IFRS-16 9.0%, still below FY2021-22's 9.3-10.1%), dividends resume under the 70% policy, and the market re-rates a $400m+ ex-lease EV. Requires several independent things to go right (macro, competition, execution), hence the 20% weight.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected interim owner FCF and exiting in year 10 earns a 15% IRR; terminal value REBUILT at the hurdle rate (min(Gordon@15%, 12x FCF_10), floored at zero) per owner-fcf.md s4; net debt and NCI deducted; probability-weighted across scenarios.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_10)). The 10% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth (base terminal 2.0% +/-1pp in 0.5pp steps). Terminal value = max(0, min(Gordon, 12x FCF_10)) in every cell.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: interest-cover covenants have been amended twice (FY25 and again for FY26/FY27), FY2025 adjusted NPAT was a loss, no dividend is being paid, the balance sheet has $93m of bank debt against a business whose lease-adjusted EBITDA is $57m, and the two structural threats (Kmart roll-out, Temu/Shein) are independent of the cycle. Bull cut to 20% because it needs macro recovery, competitive share-hold AND cost-reset execution simultaneously. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide (SBC nil in FY2025), so the accounting-regime band collapses to a point and band_position is n/a.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

valuation_philosophy.basis: Owner FCF: cash a private owner could take out after paying every lease in cash, reinvesting enough capex to sustain the store base, and paying full NZ tax once the losses are used.
key_judgments: Lease-adjusted EBITDA margin recovers only part-way to mid-cycle (3.2% base vs 4.0% median; guided cost-out is ~$17m/yr).
Capex cannot stay at $12.6m; every scenario returns it to ~1.7-2.0% of sales.
Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF (cyclical, structurally challenged); the base case binds on the cap.
Bear case is a covenant/going-concern path and is weighted 30%.

methodology: owner-fcf.md (dcf-methods skill), lease treatment (B), 10-year horizon, end-of-year discounting, TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 12x FCF_10)), entry price with TV rebuilt at the 15% hurdle.
